name: Shipping chokepoints
summary: Iran says four tankers hit mines in Hormuz on 11–12 Nov; transits still limited to routes Tehran authorises
state: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two supertankers were disabled on 11 Nov on what it called an unauthorised route, and its army said two more hit mines in the eastern strait on 12 Nov; Reuters could not verify the claims (Business Recorder, 13 Nov). UKMTO reported a vessel hit by a projectile off Ras Al-Khaimah on 11 Nov. Tehran still restricts transits to routes it authorises, while the US runs a naval blockade of Iranian ports (Euronews, 11 Nov). At least 10 ships were hit in 1–10 Nov.
for_you: Shipping through the Gulf faces rerouting, delays and higher insurance costs, which tend to feed through to fuel and freight prices. Travellers to the region should check FCDO travel advice.
rubric_hit: Hormuz traffic materially impeded: transits restricted by Iran, 4 tankers reported hit 11–12 Nov (Alert)

sources.title: Business Recorder (Reuters) — Four tankers struck by explosions in Hormuz: Iran
Euronews — Oil prices rise as investors monitor shipping disruption in the Strait of Hormuz

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
